clue.text: It causes delay in engagement, but nothing replaces a kiss

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter is swapped out of the word for a different one

parts.note: a military engagement is a battle
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
the letter taken out
to neck is to kiss, informally

explanation.surface: A delayed engagement and a couple who refuse to kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests a betrothal and 'kiss' fits it, but the engagement is a fight; the letter swap happens inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow stretch where traffic or work piles up holds everything else back, so it is a cause of hold-ups.

clue.text: Seeing that live bit of unexploded canister outside

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: one word sits outside, wrapping around the letter before it

parts.note: a canister is a case or container

indicators.note: only a small piece of the following word is wanted, namely its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of unexploded

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal scene: live ordnance with an unexploded canister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective about the bomb, but it is the verb meaning to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions giving a reason: 'seeing that it rained' and 'because it rained' mean the same.

clue.text: One looking for business needs right inside angle for it? One might

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for one looking for business

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, for tickets or a racing tip
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tout hunting for business, considering angling for it.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TOUT, giving TROUT. 'Inside' points to the placement too; 'angle' is the fishing verb, not a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers fish for this freshwater game fish, so it is something one might angle for.

clue.text: Left effects overthrow of Right and topples Tory

indicators.note: an overthrow upends things, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political headline: the Right is overthrown and the Tories topple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political next to Right and Tory, but here it means left behind, and effects are belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost property is belongings, or effects, that people have left behind and not reclaimed.

clue.text: Invaders from north or Home Counties people?

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
taken as written
the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England
men are people

explanation.surface: Asking whether invaders came from the north or from the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were Viking raiders from Scandinavia who attacked and settled in Britain and beyond.

clue.text: Emperor raised drink in saloon?

indicators.note: one word is placed in the middle of the next

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, hence the question mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the drink is a slang name for the sea

explanation.surface: An emperor raising his glass in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar to drink in, but it is a car; 'the drink' is a jokey name for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, after Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Some may be found in cafe, working

indicators.note: the answer is located inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Some people can be found in a cafe, working on laptops.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a small number of things or people, as in 'some biscuits' or 'a few biscuits'.

clue.text: They're seen with a smile, on making English supporter welcome

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word takes the others inside it

parts.note: forth means onward, as in 'from that day forth'
E is the abbreviation for English
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Greeting an English supporter with a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: FORTH takes in E and TEE: FOR(E TEE)TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Front teeth, the incisors, are the ones shown when someone smiles.

clue.text: When to work in way that's alarming Germany

indicators.note: the following words are put in the middle of the word after them

parts.note: taken as written
eek is a cry of alarm
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A worried look at how hard the Germans work.
explanation.walkthrough: D stands for Germany as its international car registration letter, from Deutschland.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday to Friday are the normal working days, as opposed to the weekend.

clue.text: Angry father is an ass, possibly

definitions.note: an ass is an example; mules and hinnies are donkey crosses

parts.note: cross means angry
to father offspring is to breed them

explanation.surface: Someone furious that their father is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun, a parent, but it is the verb meaning to beget. 'Ass' looks like an insult but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbreed is an animal bred from two different kinds; the ass, often crossed with a horse, is offered as a possible example.

clue.text: Available for touching base on Friday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first parts come after the last

parts.note: F is a short abbreviation for Friday
re means touching, concerning
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Someone saying they are available to touch base, to get in contact, on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching base' reads as one business phrase, but the two words are separate pieces: touching as concerning, and base as a mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free is available, with no other commitments to stop them.

clue.text: How to stop shoe rubbing for mum

definitions.meaning: literal sense: wear something soft over the foot inside the shoe

definitions.note: mum is an adjective meaning silent; the answer is an order to be silent
definitions.meaning: second sense: silent, as in 'keep mum'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it means silent; the phrase is a rude way to tell someone to stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase tells someone to shut up, that is, to go mum or quiet; read literally, a sock prevents chafing.

clue.text: Above acceptable temperature during explosion

parts.note: U, for upper class, means socially acceptable

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within it, so one letter goes inside a word

parts.note: a pop is a small explosion
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A warning that something is above a safe temperature and about to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: U for acceptable comes from the old 'U and non-U' labels for upper-class and lower-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Up top means overhead or in the upper part, the same as above.

clue.text: Estimated 100 rather than 50 left

indicators.note: one thing chosen rather than another means it is put in the other's place

parts.note: to evaluate something is to estimate its worth
C is the Roman numeral for 100
L is the Roman numeral for 50, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A statistic: an estimated hundred, not fifty, have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for 100 takes the place of the L for 50 in EVALUATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Evacuated means moved out of a place, so people who evacuated have left it.

clue.text: Travelling west, the other old boy's horse gets last scrap of forage from food crates

indicators.note: west is leftward on a map, so in an across clue everything reads from right to left

parts.note: 'a bit of the other' is coy British slang for sex
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

indicators.note: the final bit of the following word, its closing letter, is all that is kept

parts.note: last letter of forage

explanation.surface: An old boy's horse travelling west and getting the last bit of feed from crates.
explanation.walkthrough: SEX, OB, GG and E are read backwards. 'The other' as sex is British euphemism; an old boy is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg boxes are cartons that hold eggs, so they are containers for food; crates is a loose plural.

clue.text: Fighter sounds like a burly sort

indicators.note: a word that sounds like another is spelt differently but said the same way

parts.note: a gorilla is slang for a big burly man

explanation.surface: A boxer said to resemble a heavily built man.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is a member of an irregular armed band fighting a stronger force.

clue.text: Got maybe cold out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone caught a chill by going outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got' looks like a verb for catching a cold, but it is the definition, meaning obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to obtain or acquire it, which is what got means.

clue.text: Jangly ringtone air's principal composer?

indicators.note: a jangly sound is jarring and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tinny ringtone tune, and a question about who wrote the melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' and 'composer' suggest a tune and its writer, but composer here means a component of the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas makes up about 78 per cent of the atmosphere, so it is the main component of what we breathe.

clue.text: One makes beer in bronze jug

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for bronze
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Someone serving home-brewed beer in a bronze jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer is a person or company whose business is producing ale or lager.

clue.text: Half sub-edited without confidence

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A timid sub-editor who has only done half the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' looks like an instruction to take half of something, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashful means shy, lacking the self-assurance to speak up.

clue.text: Bounce wildly thrice, round round and around

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the scrambled letters wrap the next pair
something done wildly is uncontrolled, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape is an O
C is short for circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: Something bouncing about wildly, three times round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' wraps the jumble of thrice around the O and C from the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a rebound of a bullet or stone off a surface, so it is a bounce.

clue.text: Buff presidential contender almost gives you the screaming abdabs?

definitions.note: the screaming abdabs is a plural-looking idiom for one fit of nerves or rage

indicators.note: almost all of something means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: buff and tan are both light brown shades
Donald Trump ran for US president

explanation.surface: A presidential candidate, seen buff, alarms everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP loses its last letter. The screaming abdabs is British slang for a fit of hysteria or anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of rage, close to the hysterical fit the British slang describes.

clue.text: Guide the lady into Cheltenham?

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside

parts.note: Cheltenham is a spa town, an example, hence the question mark
the lady is her

explanation.surface: Guiding a woman into the town of Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English town famous for its mineral springs, so it stands for the general word, with a question mark for the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famous as mountain guides and porters on climbing expeditions.

clue.text: Street artist taking bit of rest in bed after accident

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: just a small piece of the next word is used, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of rest
an etcher is an artist who makes etchings

explanation.surface: A street artist resting in bed after a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist takes R at its front, after the ST for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a portable frame on which the injured are carried, a makeshift bed for accident victims.

clue.text: Legendary king given present by knight

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the present is now
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A legendary king receives a gift from his knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it is the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legendary is famous and widely recognised, so it is well known.

clue.text: Oddball's out and about

definitions.note: used as an adjective meaning eccentric

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An eccentric person is out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means unusual and eccentric, so an outré idea is an oddball one.

clue.text: Flog lad regularly, resulting in collapse

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A boy is beaten regularly until he collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold is to give way or fail, as a business or a player under pressure does.

clue.text: False reporting about old, old man

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next one
false means wrong, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Fake news about an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is informal for father, not an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is a parent or ancestor, and old man is slang for one's father.

clue.text: One inventing musical instrument listened to harp backing

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from end to start
what is listened to is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a lyre is an ancient harp-like instrument
to harp on and to rail both mean to complain persistently

explanation.surface: Someone making up a story about hearing a harp played.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes give the same answer: the sound of the instrument, and RAIL read backwards. 'Harp' looks like the instrument but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar invents falsehoods, so someone who makes things up is one.

clue.text: Standard couple of courses

parts.note: the main is the principal course of a meal
a stream is a watercourse

explanation.surface: A standard meal of two courses.
explanation.walkthrough: The two courses are of different kinds: one on a dinner menu, one that water flows along.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the conventional, normal current of opinion, the standard view.
